note: Convenience only. Detection is fully automatic (see docs/DETECTION.md) - these entries just help users find an executable. No profile paths or URL schemes are stored; both are derived at run time. An app can be removed from this file with no functional change, and an app that is NOT in it works identically via Browse.
notAPromise: Presence here does not mean an app is supported, and absence does not mean it isn't. Only the step-5 launch test decides, by starting the app once against a throwaway profile. Do not use this file as a compatibility matrix.
hintNote: Hints are directories to look for exeName in. A '*' segment matches one directory level, newest first by numeric version. Landing on a launcher stub is not fatal - LauncherStub.Resolve redirects Squirrel stubs to the real app-<version> executable - but a hint that points at the real thing saves the user a step. Store apps cannot be found by enumerating WindowsApps (a normal process may traverse it but not list it); PackageIndex reads their install paths from MrtCache instead.
provenance: measured = the launch probe was run against a real install on a real machine, and the hint resolved. inferred = the layout follows a known installer convention but has never been run here. Treat inferred hints as a guess that costs the user one Browse if wrong.

Launch test PASSED 9 Aug 2026 against Kimi 3.1.7 at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Kimi\Kimi.exe. It honours --user-data-dir and created a separate profile where it was told to, so two accounts work. Electron beyond doubt: app.asar, icudtl.dat, resources.pak, both chrome_*_percent.pak, v8_context_snapshot.bin and LICENSES.chromium.html all present; existing profile at %APPDATA%\kimi-desktop. It claims TWO schemes, kimi:// and kimi-work://, both registered as 'Kimi.exe -- "%1"'. Note the -- separator, and note that a vendor shipping a second 'work' scheme may already have an account split of its own; taking over kimi:// leaves kimi-work:// alone. Routing and badging are still untested end to end, so verified stays false - the same bar Slack is held to.
